items.title: Kerala High Court sets 2-week deadline for its judges to decide bail petitions
items.summary: The Kerala High Court has set time limits for adjudication of regular and anticipatory bail applications filed before the High Court by accused in criminal cases. According to a notice issued on September 10, the Chief Justice has set an upper time limit of 2 weeks to dispose of regular bail applications. Time granted for counsel to get instructions in regular bail matters shall not be allowed to exceed 7 working days. For anticipatory bail applications, the maximum time for disposal has been set at 6 weeks. The notice was issued in line with the Supreme Court's May 11 order which directed High Courts to take steps to speed up bail hearings. Set deadlines, say no to adjournments: Supreme Court directs High Courts to speed up bail hearings [Read Notice] Kerala High Court sets 2-week deadline for its judges to decide bail petitions report by @GitiPratap https://t.co/rzlV8ZFr4O — Bar and Bench (@barandbench) September 11, 2026

items.title: Plea before Kerala High Court seeks disqualification of MLA Mani C Kappan after cheque bounce conviction
items.summary: A petition has been filed before the Kerala High Court seeking the disqualification of Member of Legislative Assembly (MLA) Mani C Kappan following his conviction earlier this month in a cheque dishonour case. [ Dinesh Menon v. State of Kerala & Ors. ] On September 1, a Mumbai court convicted Pala MLA Kappan in four cases under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, and sentenced him to a cumulative three and a half years of simple imprisonment. He was also ordered to pay ₹5.30 crores as compensation to the complainant in all four cases, businessman Dinesh Menon. The petition seeking Kappan's disqualification was filed before the High Court by Menon himself. In his petition, Menon has submitted that the order of the Mumbai court does not state that the sentences are to run concurrently. He has argued that as per legal precedents, upon conviction and impostition of sentence of over two years, sitting MLAs are to be immediately disqualified. However, Kappan continues to hold his position and no formal notification has been issued declaring his seat vacant. items.title: Delhi High Court slams Punjab & Sind Bank for denying reward to manager who foiled robbery in 1998
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently directed the Punjab & Sind Bank to pay an amount of ₹50,000, along with an annual interest of 12 percent, to a manager who had foiled a robbery attempt at its Najafgarh Branch in 1998 [ Surjit Singh Vs Punjab & Sind Bank] . Justice Neena Bansal Krishna also awarded litigation costs of ₹2 lakh to the manager, Surjit Singh, while taking exception to the management’s conduct of making him suffer litigation for 28 years over compensation for his bravery. The Court said that instead of the bank and the government itself rewarding Singh in accordance with the relevant guidelines, they added insult to injury by asserting that his act was not covered by the guidelines. "Such conduct is not becoming of the Bank, which itself, in fact, should have rewarded and acknowledged the Petitioner for his exemplary conduct, rather than driving him to seek reward to which he was entitled. It has taken him since 28 years to get the validation of his act," the Court said. The Court added that the question was not of money but of the honour, which should have come to him on its own without litigation. items.title: Girl had accused’s name tattooed on her chest: Delhi High Court reduces rape convict’s sentence
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has reduced the sentence of a man convicted of rape and kidnapping a 14-year-old girl after noting that she had his name tattooed on her chest and had voluntarily travelled with him to Manali. [Vakul Kapoor Vs State] Justice Vimal Kumar Yadav said the circumstances indicated that the two were in an “amorous relationship”, though the girl’s age meant that the relationship could not legally be recognised. Therefore, the Court held that the nearly two years and four months already undergone by the man in custody would be sufficient punishment. The Court particularly referred to the tattoos and the girl’s conduct. “ Deep down somewhere, she must also be looking for answers and explanation for the tattoos and travel to Manali, etc, ” the Court observed. Justice VIMAL KUMAR YADAV and Delhi HC The case arose from an incident in June 2009. The girl, then around 14, went missing from her home and travelled with the convict, who was around 18, first to Connaught Place and thereafter to Manali. They returned to Delhi two days later. items.title: No offence of rape on promise of marriage when victim and accused already married to other people: HP High Court
items.summary: The Himachal Pradesh High Court recently held that a promise of marriage may not amount to the offence of deceitful sexual intercourse when both the accused and the victim are already married to other people and were aware of each other’s marital status [Vinod Kumar v State of Himachal Pradesh] . Justice Sandeep Sharma made the observation while granting bail to one Vinod Kumar, an astrologer, accused of sexually assaulting a 31-year-old woman on the alleged promise of marriage. In the order dated September 3, the Court noted that both the accused and the woman were married to other people and neither had divorced their respective spouses. It therefore found that there was prima facie no question of a promise to marry. "There was no question of promise to marry, especially when factum of marriage of the petitioner as well victim/prosecutrix was in the know of the victim/prosecutrix as well as bail petitioner. Once victim/prosecutrix as well as petitioner had not taken divorce from their respective spouses, they otherwise could not have solemnize marriage," held the Court. items.title: Karnataka High Court pulls up advocates for not paying process fee years after securing interim order
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Thursday took strong exception to the practice of not paying the process fees in cases where interim orders had been passed months or even years earlier. Justice V Srishananda said the Court would not tolerate litigants obtaining interim orders and then allowing the cases to remain pending for years. “Don't think otherwise. I am harsh, I am required to be harsh. We cannot tolerate this. Taking an interim order and managing an internet copy, how is this?” the Court told an advocate. The judge warned that he will vacate the interim orders in the cases where process fee was yet to be paid. “Take your sweet time. A 2026 matter will reflect only in 2036," Justice Srishananda quipped. Justice V Srishananda The Court was hearing a matter where the process fee had not been paid despite an order dated March 9, 2026. When the advocate cited oversight as the reason, the judge warned that he will dismiss the case. Justice Srishananda said he had come across several cases dating back to 2021 where process fees had not been paid. “I have cases from 2021. They have not paid the fee. I have 100 cases. items.title: Delhi High Court refuses to restrain Xiaomi from using ‘Find Device’ feature in its mobile phones
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on September 7 refused to restrain Xiaomi Technology India from using its “Find Device” feature in its mobile phones after finding that it did not prima facie infringe a patent for technology designed to recover stolen mobile phones [Conqueror innovation Vs Xiaomi]. A bench of Justices V Kameswar Rao and Manmeet Pritam Singh Arora dismissed an appeal filed by Conqueror Innovations Private Limited and the inventor of the patented “Communication Device Finder System” (appellants). The appeal challenged a July 2025 order of a single-judge refusing them interim relief against Xiaomi. The Court upheld the finding that Xiaomi’s system did not contain the essential features of the patented technology. “ We therefore uphold the findings of the learned Single Judge that the Appellants have failed to establish a prima facie case of infringement of the suit patent, ” the Court said. Justice V Kameswar Rao and Justice Manmeet Pritam Singh Arora According to the appellants, the invention was conceived after the inventor lost 152 mobile phones in a burglary in 2004. items.title: Assets worth ₹14,131 crore given to banks but PMLA charges against Vijay Mallya will stay: ED to Bombay HC
items.summary: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has told the Bombay High Court that recovery of assets for banks from businessman Vijay Mallya does not absolve him of the pending money laundering charges [Vijay Vittal Mallya v. State Bank of India & Ors] The submission was made in response to a Court order directing the ED and the State Bank of India-led consortium of lenders to ascertain whether Mallya’s attached properties had cleared his debts. In an affidavit filed on September 8, the ED said that movable and immovable properties worth ₹14,131.6 crores (as in August 2021) stand handed over to the SBI-led consortium. However, the ED said that the recovery by itself does not cancel or lead to the dropping of the money laundering charges against Mallya. The agency argued that restoring assets under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) is a statutory mechanism for legitimate claimants to recover their losses. “The criminal prosecution launched pursuant to the investigation under the PMLA is therefore not rendered infructuous merely because the claimant banks have subsequently recovered substantial amounts from the assets restored to them,” the agency said. items.title: Supreme Court flags gaps in FSSAI plan for red-hexagon warning labels on foods high in fat, sugar, salt
items.summary: The Supreme Court on September 10 flagged several gaps in the FSSAI’s proposal for hexagon shaped warning labels on packaged foods high in sugar, salt and fat [ 3S And Our Health Society v. Union of India & Anr. ]. A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran sought a timeline for introducing the labels and questioned the proposed two-phase rollout, particularly the plan to initially cover only products high in at least two of sugar, salt and fat rather than all products high in any one of these nutrients. The Bench gave the FSSAI 10 days to respond and posted the matter for further hearing on September 28. Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice Vinod Chandran The Court was hearing a public interest litigation (PIL) plea seeking the display of warning labels on packaged food items to indicate their salt, sugar and fat levels. During an earlier hearing, the Bench had criticised the FSSAI’s handling of the issue and questioned whether the regulator was bowing to corporate pressure instead of acting on a matter concerning public health, particularly the health of children. items.title: Religious conversion: Allahabad HC orders police to produce Ayush Malik after plea claims illegal detention by family
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court has directed authorities in Uttar Pradesh to produce Ayush Malik before the Court on a plea alleging that he has been kept in illegal custody by his family after he converted to Islam and married a Muslim woman [Ayush Malik and Another v State of UP and 3 Others] Malik's conversion from Hinduism to Islam had led to the arrest of the Muslim woman Chandni Qureshi and her father under the Uttar Pradesh Prohibition of Unlawful Conversion of Religion Act, 2021 in a case registered by Shamli police. Malik, who had changed his name to Mohammad Ali, had told the media that he had converted to Islam voluntarily. However, his businessman father claimed that he was coerced by the Muslim woman and her family to gain control over their property. Malik later reportedly returned to Hinduism. In a fresh twist to the story, a habeas corpus petition before the High Court states that Malik's father has deprived him of his personal liberty and kept him in illegal custody with the active assistance of the State machinery. items.title: Parties don't trust institutions yet: Mihir Thakore on why ad-hoc arbitration still wins in India
items.summary: The Gujarat High Court Arbitration Centre (GHAC) recently conducted a 3-day Arbitration Week 2026 at GIFT City Club, Gandhinagar The event brought together the judiciary, lawyers and arbitration practitioners to chart the future of institutional arbitration in India. On the sidelines of the event, Bar & Bench's Pallavi Saluja spoke with Senior Advocate Mihir Thakore on the state of Indian arbitration a decade after the 2015 amendments, the persistent trust deficit around institutional arbitration and why Ahmedabad's arbitration ambitions may struggle to move beyond the domestic market. Edited excerpts follow. [Watch Video] Pallavi Saluja (PS): Indian arbitration has undergone a significant change over the past decade. From your perspective, what has genuinely improved since the 2015 amendments and what reforms do we still need to make? Senior Advocate Mihir Thakore For arbitrations commenced after 2015, it still takes at least 3 years to conclude once pleadings are over, which is not a good sign. Mihir Thakore (MT): To some extent, there is an improvement in the timelines by which arbitration is getting over. I can’t say it's a huge improvement, but there is a marginal improvement.
